segments.t: KorTTY records terminal sessions as lightweight replay files with optional color capture and video export. Session recordings capture screen-state changes and timing events without continuous pixel capture, making them efficient and portable.
Terminal recording saves session data into compressed JSONL replay files, one per terminal tab session:
KTPH001Legacy formatKTPH002: KTPH000 files remain readable (uncompressed)
KTPH000ContentKTPH001: Screen-state changes, timing events, and optional color runs
KTPH000VideoKTPH001: Never recorded directly; WebM/VP9 and MKV/FFV1 files come only from KTPH002exporting a replayKTPH003
Recordings do not continuously capture pixels and do not stream over the network. File size depends on activity level and whether color capture is enabled.
To make recording available after every app restart:
Enable KTPH000Enable terminal recording after app restartKTPH001
To enable recording only until KorTTY quits:
Select KTPH000Enable terminal recording for this app sessionKTPH001
In KTPH000Tools KTPH002 Video ManagerKTPH001, set these options:
Directory where replay files are saved (default: KTPH000)
Record active split only or entire tab
Pause recording when terminal is inactive
Include per-cell terminal style runs in new recordings
Path to local KTPH000 binary for video export

Enable color capture KTPH000beforeKTPH001 recording if you want exported videos to reproduce terminal colors accurately. Existing recordings without color data can still export, but colors won't be preserved.
Video export requires a local KTPH000 installation:
In KTPH001Tools KTPH003 Video ManagerKTPH002, enter the full path to KTPH000 (or leave blank to auto-detect)
If KTPH000 is not found, video export remains disabled but replay viewing and other features work normally
On macOS and Linux, if KTPH000 is in your PATH, KorTTY auto-detects it. On Windows, you may need to provide the full path.
Open or focus an SSH terminal tab
If recording is enabled, click KTPH000Start recordingKTPH001 in the terminal bar, or:
Choose KTPH000Tools KTPH002 Start/Stop Terminal RecordingKTPH001, or
If the tab contains split terminals, choose:
KTPH000Active splitKTPH001 — record only the focused terminal pane
KTPH000Entire tabKTPH001 — record all visible splits
The terminal bar control is hidden until recording is enabled or the menu item/shortcut is used.
Click KTPH000Stop recordingKTPH001 in the terminal bar, or
Start and stop recording as often as needed within the same tab. All segments append to the same replay file until the tab closes. Each recording start/stop creates a new segment in the file.
Exported videos require KTPH000 to be available and configured.
Verify that KTPH000ffmpeg statusKTPH001 says video export is enabled
Choose KTPH000Export entire recordingKTPH001 or specify a custom time range
For custom ranges, enter start/end times as KTPH000 (minutes) or KTPH001 (minutes and seconds)
Values past the replay duration are rejected
Choose whether to KTPH000Include terminal colorsKTPH001 (available only if the replay contains color data)
Select output format: KTPH000WebM/VP9KTPH001 or KTPH002MKV/FFV1KTPH003
During export, a progress dialog shows:
Export uses the recorded terminal geometry to avoid cropping wide terminal screens. If the geometry is not available, KorTTY computes a legacy fallback size.
Click KTPH000ViewKTPH001 to open the replay in the built-in viewer
KTPH000Timeline sliderKTPH001 — Drag to jump to any position
KTPH002Time jumpKTPH003 — Enter KTPH000 for minute 5, KTPH001 for 5 minutes 30 seconds
KTPH000SpeedKTPH001 — Set playback speed between 1x and 20x
Select a replay in KTPH000Tools KTPH002 Video ManagerKTPH001
The file is renamed in the storage folder
Select a replay in KTPH000Tools KTPH002 Video ManagerKTPH001
Replay files contain timestamped events in JSONL format (one event per line, gzip-compressed). The decompressed JSONL may contain:
Screen-state change (may include KTPH000 with foreground/background values)
Each screen event includes terminal content, dimensions, and optional color style runs. Text inside a clickable OSC 8 link is recorded with the colors, bold and inverse video it was printed with.
KTPH000Large terminal windowsKTPH001: Terminal geometry is recorded, so wide screens export correctly without cropping
KTPH000Color accuracyKTPH001: Enable color capture before recording if you plan to export video with terminal colors
KTPH000Idle pauseKTPH001: Auto-pause helps reduce file size during long idle periods; enable it unless you need to preserve exact timing
KTPH000Split-scope selectionKTPH001: Choose your recording scope (active split vs. entire tab) each time you start recording to match your workflow
KTPH001Legacy filesKTPH002: Old KTPH000 (uncompressed) replay files are still readable in the Video Manager
